newsitem.title: USA: Rambus shares jump 150 percent in debut.
newsitem.headline: Rambus shares jump 150 percent in debut.

text.p: Rambus Inc's shares jumped by about 150 percent on its first trading day, proving that the market is as pleased with the company as the technical community is with its product, Rambus executives said.
"The reception of the financial community parallels the reception of the technical community for Rambus and we are obviously very delighted," Rambus chief financial officer Gary Harmon told Reuters.
Shares of Rambus vaulted to $30-1/4 a share, up $18-1/4, on volume of about 5.16 million shares. Earlier, its indication was raised to $10 to $12 a share from $8 to $10 a share.

Rambus licenses its technology to a majority of the world's top memory-chip makers. The technology speeds the graphics handling capacity of PCs by processing data up to four times faster than current chips.
It said its largest contracts are held by Toshiba Corp, NEC Corp and LG Group's LG Semicon unit. Other customers include Intel Corp, Hitachi Ltd and Mitsubishi Electric Corp.

The company declined to discuss growth projections due to a quiet period following its offering, but it noted that in 1996, sales of chips made by others that incorporated Rambus' technology totaled $477 million, up from $13 million in 1995.
Last autumn, Rambus Chief Executive Geoff Tate said the company plans to see Rambus-based memory chips form a majority of world production in 2000.

Harmon said the company gets a royalty percentage on each Rambus-based chip sold. On sales of dynamic random access memory (DRAMs) chips, the maximum royalty is 2.5 percent, while on sales of logic chips, the maximum royalty is 5.0 percent.
Rambus' technology allows DRAM chips to transfer data significantly faster than other available techniques.
"Comparable technologies are developed by the chip companies themselves, but there is nothing that operates at the frequency that we do," said Subodh Tobrani, vice president of marketing for Rambus.
"(Other chips) are operating at 66 Megahertz (clock cycles per second), or even struggling to get to 100 Mhz," he added. "Our technology is currently shipping from some of our licensees at 600 MHz."
Rambus' investors include Microsoft Corp Chairman Bill Gates and Dell Computer Corp founder and Chairman Michael Dell.
